clue.text: Wife leaving Jack the Lad for dedicated follower of fashion

indicators.note: the wife walks out on the lad, so her letter goes from the word for him

parts.note: a whipster is an old word for a cocky, lively young fellow

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on her flashy husband for a man who follows every trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack the Lad' is British slang for a brash, swaggering young man; 'dedicated follower of fashion' quotes a Kinks song.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend-chasing, self-consciously stylish person is the modern sense of the word.

clue.text: Unusually hard arrow traced to 14's finder

definitions.note: 14 across is the boy pharaoh whose tomb this English Egyptologist uncovered in 1922

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the two words are put together in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A strangely firm arrow points the way to a discoverer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges ARROW TRACED; H for hard comes first, unscrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: The British archaeologist who discovered the pharaoh's tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

clue.text: Reminder for politician to attend closing of parliament

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A note for an MP to attend the end of a parliamentary session.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue or nudge to jog the memory, as given to an actor, is a reminder.

clue.text: Press employee temporarily on vacation to exercise dog

indicators.note: vacated, the word is emptied of its inside, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker, briefly on holiday, takes the dog for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' reads as on holiday but means emptying 'temporarily' to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets type for printing works for a printing press.

clue.text: Bank upset over money transfer

indicators.note: the reversed bank lies over and around the money letter
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A bank is unhappy about a transfer of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TIER to REIT, which goes around M.
explanation.definitionFit: To send money, or pass a matter on to an authority, is to transfer it.

clue.text: Band with penny at the end in small amount of prize money

indicators.note: the shifted band sits inside the word for a small amount

parts.note: a jot is a tiny amount, as in 'not a jot'

indicators.note: the penny's letter is shifted from the front of the band's word to its tail

parts.note: a pack is a band of wolves or people

explanation.surface: A musical group gets a penny at the end of the night, a pitiful share of the winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a pack, as of wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: The top prize in a lottery or game, the pot of winnings, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Drink containing calcium and root of acacia tree

indicators.note: the drink holds the calcium symbol inside

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, as in 'a quick jar'
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

indicators.note: a word's root is its beginning, its first letter

explanation.surface: A drink fortified with calcium and acacia root.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical American tree with blue-violet blossom, planted for ornament.

clue.text: Actor died having lost odd set of principles

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are lost, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An actor dies after losing his peculiar collection of beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd set' looks like a strange collection but means the first, third, fifth letters and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of rules or standards of conduct, as in a moral code, is a set of principles.

clue.text: Girl supported by both parents has a broad outlook

indicators.note: the girl is held up on either side by her parents, one each side

parts.note: pa and ma are father and mother
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl backed by her mother and father takes a wide view of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide, sweeping view or survey of a scene or subject is a broad outlook.

clue.text: Men trial new marking on tennis court

indicators.note: a new version of the words reorders their letters

explanation.surface: Male players try out a fresh painted line at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: The parallel side lines marking a doubles alley on a tennis court are called this.

clue.text: Cheer when doctor visits surgery

indicators.note: the doctor calls at the surgery, so the two sit side by side, doctor first

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the BBC series
OP is short for operation, a piece of surgery

explanation.surface: A patient gives a shout of joy when the doctor drops in at the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'surgery' is also a doctor's consulting room, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry of delight or excitement is a shout of cheer, the noun sense.

clue.text: Comedian sacked by head of austere region of Greece

indicators.note: a city that is sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A comic is fired by a stern boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' reads as dismissed but signals the letters of COMEDIAN being rearranged into MACEDONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is the large northern administrative area of the Greek mainland around Thessaloniki.

clue.text: Agent with old anecdote about one in vault

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: the anecdote goes around the letter for one

parts.note: an anecdote is a short story
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A salesman spins an old yarn about someone down in a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is a place where things are stored for safekeeping, a store or depository.

clue.text: Verbal leaders of outspoken rabble are lefties

indicators.note: the leaders of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: The ringleaders of a loud mob turn out to be left-wingers who talk a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written: verbal in its sense of by word of mouth.

clue.text: Waste 11 with slight convexity around top of handle and upturned lid

definitions.note: 11 across is a repository, so a repository for waste

indicators.note: the convexity goes around the handle's top letter

parts.note: camber is the slight upward curve of a road surface

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
upturned in a down clue means the word is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: a top is a lid

explanation.surface: A curved vessel for waste with a handle and a lid turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom bowl kept for night-time use is a receptacle for bodily waste.

clue.text: Vessel containing another meat socially acceptable for ancient king

indicators.note: the first vessel holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
another vessel: a tank holds liquid
ham is cured pork
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A dish of one container inside another, with posh ham, fit for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows the noun from 'Vessel' to mean a second vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy pharaoh of Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty, famous for his intact tomb, was a king of antiquity.

clue.text: Drug rejected by learner in struggle to be excellent

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the drug's word reads backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: the learner goes inside the struggle

parts.note: a fight is a struggle
L is the learner-driver sign

explanation.surface: A trainee rejects drugs in a battle to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate, of the highest class, is excellent.

clue.text: Easy setter — female — in run-of-the-mill setting

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

indicators.note: the female goes inside the run-of-the-mill word, its setting

parts.note: normal means ordinary, run-of-the-mill

explanation.surface: A relaxed setter, a woman, in an ordinary setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and casual, easy in manner, is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Doctor sees about fastener for shrouds

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about the fastener
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: a clip is a fastener

explanation.surface: A doctor checks on a fastener for burial cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' makes ESES from its word, and 'about' wraps that round the fastener. 'shrouds' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure or overshadow something, as the moon hides the sun, is to shroud it.

clue.text: Part of cell released by sumac pollen

indicators.note: the letters are set free from the two words and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is set free from the pollen of a sumac shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The protoplasm inside a cell's nucleus is a component of that cell.

clue.text: See 1 down
Simple introduction to solutions to be found in a grid

definitions.text: Simple introduction to solutions to be found in a grid

parts.note: light means simple, not heavy or demanding

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An easy beginner's guide to answers that go into a crossword grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In crossword jargon the entries that fill a grid are known as its lights.

clue.text: God right to desert French artist?

indicators.note: right walks out, so its letter leaves the artist's name

parts.note: Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: Was it right for someone to abandon a French artist?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a sculptor is called an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Norse mythology, one-eyed lord of Asgard.

clue.text: Refuse to be taken in by swaggering gait of the fashionable set

indicators.note: the rubbish is absorbed by the reworked walk, sitting inside it
a swaggering walk lurches about, so the letters of the walk are thrown around

parts.note: litter is rubbish, refuse

explanation.surface: Trash is hidden by the strutting walk of trendy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swaggering' makes GATI, and 'to be taken in by' puts the rubbish after its first letter. 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities and socialites who glitter, the smart crowd, are this set.

clue.text: Take supplement primarily found in fish bones

indicators.note: the two letters are placed inside the fish

parts.note: the tai is a red sea bream
R is from Latin recipe, take, as written on prescriptions

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter

explanation.surface: Take a supplement, found mainly in fish, for your bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of small bones in the ankle or insect's foot: tarsals.

clue.text: Construction materials impounded by sensible government

indicators.note: the letters are locked up inside the two words

explanation.surface: Building supplies seized by a prudent administration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish plastic interlocking bricks are toy building materials.

clue.text: Predicament encountered by awfully green go-between …

parts.note: a mess is a predicament, a difficult fix

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of green are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naive envoy finds himself in a real fix.
explanation.definitionFit: One who carries messages between parties is an intermediary or go-between.

clue.text: … caught en route to bed

indicators.note: en is French for in, so caught goes inside the route

parts.note: a path is a route
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The go-between is caught on the way to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from the previous clue; 'en route' reads as one phrase but 'en' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plot of garden ground, such as a vegetable plot, is a bed.

clue.text: Keep going from US city getting southern trade

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to tout is to peddle or sell, to trade in

explanation.surface: Someone moves away from an American city to go into business in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure to the end, keep going or survive, is this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Trainees in pubs covering short part of academic year

indicators.note: the pubs enclose the shortened term

parts.note: inns are pubs

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a school or university year is divided into terms

explanation.surface: Apprentices hang around in bars during part of the school year.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior doctors or students working to gain experience are trainees, especially in America.
